turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, Mrs Pillay. I'm just going to check your blood pressure and weight before the doctor calls you. Shoes off on the scale, please.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, shame, these shoes are a mission. My daughter had to help me with the laces in the car.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Right. Blood pressure is one hundred and forty-six over eighty-eight, and your pulse is seventy-four. Weight is ninety-one point five kilograms.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Ninety-one? Eish. I was eighty-something at Christmas, I think. Or was that the year before.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ma, you were already over ninety in December. Don't start.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor will see you just now. There's a chair inside.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come in, come in. Sorry, this computer is being difficult. Mrs Pillay, and this is?
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm her daughter, Priya. I brought her because the knee's been a proper problem.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay. Give me one second, the file hasn't loaded. Right. What's brought you in today?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): It's this knee, doctor. The right one. Going down the stairs at the flat it just bites, and most nights it wakes me and I have to shift around.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the screen jumped. Down the stairs, and at night. Which knee did you say?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): The right one. Left is fine, touch wood.
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's been going on for about six months, doctor. Since around the winter.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, no, Priya, it's not six months. It's more like three months, after that long weekend when we went to the coast.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): So I'm hearing three months from you and six from your daughter. I'll put roughly three to six months. We don't have to pin the date.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She won't use the lift. She says the lift smells.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): It does smell, like old cabbage. Anyway the stairs are the problem, especially coming down, not so much going up.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): And at night, is it every night?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Most nights, ja. Not every single one. It's a deep ache, right in the knee.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Does it lock, or give way under you?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No, it doesn't lock, and it hasn't given way. I just go slow.
[SEG0022] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It does puff up though. I've seen the knee swollen by the evening, especially after she's been to the shops.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): It does not swell, Priya. It just feels stiff. You're exaggerating.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hmm, you two don't agree on the swelling. I'll have a look in a minute. Any redness, or does it feel hot?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No redness. It doesn't feel hot.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again, I was typing in the wrong box.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No redness, and it's not hot to the touch.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): What have you been using for it?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): The diclofenac gel from the chemist. I rub it on the knee, morning and night. It helps a little for the stairs.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the tablets. She's been taking diclofenac tablets as well, the seventy-five milligram ones, nearly every day.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no, it's the fifty milligram tablets, and not every day. Only when it's really sore, maybe two or three times in a week. I buy them at the chemist and they don't ask for a script.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hang on, the system wants me to click something again. Fifty or seventy-five?
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The box in her cupboard says seventy-five. I looked this morning.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): That old box is from last year. The ones I'm using now are fifty. I know my own tablets.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright, I'm not going to guess the strength if you're seeing different boxes. We'll leave the dose unclear. Do you swallow them, by mouth?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, by mouth, with a bit of tea. Not on an empty stomach. My neighbour told me that.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any stomach trouble with them? Nausea, pain, black stool?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no stomach problems. My stomach is fine, doctor.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. And the gel, any rash where you put it?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No rash.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Mind you, I do get heartburn. Some evenings there's a burning here in the chest, after supper. It's been a few weeks. A sip of milk settles it a bit.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Heartburn. You just said the stomach was fine. When did the heartburn start?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know exactly when it started. A few weeks, maybe. It's not every day.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She mentioned the heartburn to me last Sunday, after the braai at my place. She had two helpings of the potato salad.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): The potato salad was lekker, don't blame the salad. And it was a nice afternoon. The little one was running around in his cricket shirt.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh, Kyle. He's mad about cricket. He told everyone he wants to open the batting one day, pads and all.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Then he asked if I watched the match, and I said only the highlights, because of the load shedding. The power came back right in the middle of the ads.
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We sat outside anyway. The weather was perfect, not a cloud, and the neighbour's dog kept trying to steal the boerewors off the grill.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): That dog is a menace. Last week it chased the postman all the way to the robot on the corner. The poor man had to wait at the light like the dog understands traffic.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, I drifted. There was an old note open on the screen. We're still on the knee, not the dog. Let me have a look.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): Bend it for me. There's crepitus in the right knee when you bend, and I can feel a small effusion. No redness, and it's not warm.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): See, Priya, a small bit of fluid, not this big swollen thing you were describing.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): It's mild. The left knee moves more freely. This right one is the problem, and with the weight at ninety-one point five the stairs are going to keep aggravating it.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): So I must lose weight. Everyone says that. I already don't take sugar in my rooibos.
[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to lecture you. Even a few kilograms would take pressure off that knee. Nothing drastic.
[SEG0056] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I've been telling her. She still wants roti twice a week.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Roti is not the enemy, my child.

[SEG0058] person_4 (DOCTOR): I think this is most likely osteoarthritis, wear and tear in the right knee, given the stairs, the night pain, and what I feel in the joint. That's a working impression, not a final diagnosis. We haven't done an x-ray.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I need an x-ray?

[SEG0060] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not today. We can think about an x-ray later if we need one. For now I'm stuck between sending you for physio and doing a steroid injection into the knee, and I don't want to decide that this visit.
[SEG0061] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Which one would you lean towards?
[SEG0062] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the night pain is still waking her in about a month, then we look at physio or the injection properly. Either might help. Nothing is booked.
[SEG0063] person_2 (PATIENT): And the gel? Can I carry on with the gel?

[SEG0064] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, carry on with the diclofenac gel morning and night. I'd rather you ease off the tablets until we know which strength you're actually taking, because of that heartburn. Don't buy more for now.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): So stop the tablets?
[SEG0066] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pause them, yes. The gel can continue. And come back in six weeks. We'll make a proper decision then.
[SEG0067] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll bring both boxes so you can see them.
[SEG0068] person_4 (DOCTOR): Please do. Reception will give you the date on the way out. And just watch those stairs, hey.
